source.source_boundary: NSIMI represents different similar items with identical data which cannot replace each other. The parent native run exposed separate similarity-index stocks but both were stocked at demand. This case seeks a demand against index 1 when its stock is empty and index 0 retains stock.

delta.mechanism: Reduce source STSIZ from 2 to 1, applied per NSIMI index, and extend direct LRU repair from one to 30 hours. Keep item NSIMI2, QTYPM1, system/item rates, missions, seed, and horizon inherited.

predeclared_native_acceptance: All author-populated source tables roundtrip, conversion errors are zero, and all five guarded steps complete with the existing GUI preserved.

The first index-1 failure consumes its sole index-1 spare. The removed item remains under direct repair when a second index-1 demand arrives; the index-1 stock is empty, while index-0 stock still holds its one spare.

The second index-1 demand remains unfilled or backordered until the observation horizon; no index-0 item is issued to that demand. Native event identities, stock levels, backorder state, mission outcomes, report bins, and terminal states must reconcile without assuming that a missing issue alone proves a prohibition.

If native evidence does not show the concurrent index-1 shortage and index-0 spare, this run is diagnostic and cannot establish the non-interchangeability boundary. All source/run hashes and raw files must be sealed and independently replayed.
limits: One aircraft, one seed, one similarity pair, one base station, 36 hours; it tests an indexed native stockout sequence, not all inventory policies or generic substitution.
The repair duration and stock size are changed together to create the boundary; any mission outcome difference is not an isolated NSIMI effect.
